Author: tholin
Content: Wait a second, my battery charge controller chip is essentially just a linear voltage regulator with a current limiter and control state machine. If you ripped out just the linear regulator part of that, couldn’t you, say, generate a 3.3V core voltage on-die and have a single 5V power supply on a digital chip using my SCL?

Author: tholin
Content: I’d have to measure the dropout on the regulator to see what the true power supply range would be and maybe come up with a way of having a selectable 3.3V/5V IO voltage (though the former would be relatively weak coming from the internal regulator).

Author: tholin
Content:
The power transistors for this would actually be quite small since the current consumption of standard cell logic, even for a dense 1x1 chip, should be pretty low. I think the full regulator could fit in a corner of the core area without taking up too much space. I’d have to use my run 2 chips to collect more data on my SCL.
If the 3.3V is also to supply the IO, it can be beefed up to 1A relatively easily while still not taking up too much space. For reference: my charge controller has a third of a 1x0p5 core area filled with just PFETs and that can conduct 110A according to SPICE. So, yeah, don’t need much FET to get 1A.
